title: Phased Capacity Sprint Simulator & Ops Mapping
content:
Purpose
This working doc defines a lightweight simulator and operational runbook to stage phased traffic ramps for new product launches and major model rollouts. The aim is to give product+ops a practical, repeatable sequence to: (1) validate capacity assumptions, (2) exercise oncall/playbook, (3) collect signal windows for automatic rollback decisions.

Scope and audience
- Audience: product managers, product ops, SRE, serving-runtime, support-runbook owners.
- Scope: initial 10k -> 1M request/day ramps for Hosted API routes and Dedicated pools. Includes traffic model, Monte Carlo stress bands, staffing map, and launch-day checklist.

Design principles (short)
- Safety-first: prefer conservative traffic steps with automated fallback triggers.
- Observability-driven: every step must produce a 30-min telemetry window used to decide next step.
- Rehearse-and-measure: run at least one full dry-run on staging with identical traffic pattern.

Simulation model overview
- Traffic distribution: Poisson baseline with burst events (25% chance per hour of +2x on 3% of requests).
- Request profile mix: 70% short-gen (<128 tokens), 25% medium (128-512), 5% long (>512).
- Service model: map request mix to CPU/GPU token-costs using conservative kernel factors (short: 1 unit, medium: 3 units, long: 8 units).
- Queueing: per-model concurrent request limit (CRL) drives queuing latency; we simulate per-pool queue length and p95 latency.
- Failover rules: if sustained 5m p95 latency > target or error rate spike > 0.8% -> mark step unhealthy.

Monte Carlo assumptions (quick)
- Run 500 trials per ramp step, sample burst probability and model mix within +/-10% noise.
- Output: median, 75th, 95th percentiles for p95 latency, token/sec throughput, queue length, error rate.

Ramp stages (recommended)
- Stage A (smoke): 0.1% traffic, soak 15m — objective: basic correctness, warm KV/prefix cache.
- Stage B (micro): 1% traffic, soak 30m — objective: baseline latency and tail behavior.
- Stage C (pilot): 5% traffic, soak 45m with simulated churn — objective: autoscaler response and cache hit-rate.
- Stage D (scale): 20% traffic, soak 60m — objective: model variant routing and multi-region failover.
- Stage E (full): remaining traffic in 2x steps, each soak 60-90m, only if prior step healthy.

Decision criteria to advance
- p95 latency <= SLO * 1.15 for the soak window (SLO example: 400ms for short-gen routes).
- Error rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (baseline taken from last 7 days).
- Autoscaler stable: no >30% thrash (scale ups/downs) in 15m window.
- Operator signoff recorded in channel #go-live (simple text reaction is enough).

Rollback/containment policy (automated + manual)
- Auto rollback triggers (immediate): sustained 5m p95 > 2x SLO OR error rate > 2% absolute.
- Containment step: throttle new sessions to safe level (e.g., 60% of prior stable step) and route to fallback model variant.
- Manual escalation: on-call SRE to page with urgency if auto rollback invoked; run triage playbook.

Operational mappings (who does what)
- PM (owner): defines traffic cohorts, customer opt-in lists, and acceptance criteria.
- Product-ops (lead): runs simulator, assembles telemetry dashboard snapshot, coordinates go/no-go and gates.
- Serving-runtime (engineer oncall): validates kernel performance, adjusts pool configs, reviews cold-start behavior.
- SRE (oncall): monitors infra SLOs, executes containment and rollbacks, and updates incident doc.
- Support (tier-1): watches customer chatter channels, triages early reports, files ops tickets.

Staffing plan per ramp (example for Stage C->D)
- Oncall window: 2 hours before Stage C start through 1 hour after Stage D completes.
- Minimum coverage: 1 SRE, 1 runtime engineer, 1 product-ops, 1 support lead, backup oncall for escalation.
- Paging rules: immediate page to SRE if p95 crosses auto-rollback threshold; otherwise Slack alert to #go-live.

Launch-day checklist (preflight)
- Confirm staging clean run: artifacts, traffic profile recorded, no open critical PRs.
- Verify runbook pinned and accessible; list of rollback commands tested in dry-run.
- Confirm model variants uploaded and hashed; cache-warm scripts available.
- Ensure quota and rate limit settings for test accounts to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Confirm paging lists and contact numbers for primary backup.

Launch-day checklist (during ramp)
- Start Stage A and post snapshot at T+15m to #go-live with key metrics: p95 latency, error rate, token/sec, queue length.
- Wait decision window (15-30m) and consult Monte Carlo heatmap in dashboard.
- If go, advance to next stage. If marginal, hold and run targeted mitigation (e.g., increase pool size by 10%).
- If fail, initiate auto-rollback and run containment checklist.

Post-launch (30/90/180m) checks
- 30m: validate tail latency receded, no customer-impact alerts from support.
- 90m: collect usage slices by cohort, compare to MC predicted percentiles, log deviations.
- 180m: handoff to steady-state ops; produce short postmortem note if any rollbacks or mitigations occurred.

Metrics lexicon (how we compute signals)
- p95 latency: measured from request submit to final token emitted for short-gen; for streaming, measure first-byte p95 and completion p95 separately.
- error rate: 5xx + 429 + timeout faults divided by total requests in window.
- token/sec: aggregated tokens across all requests divided by window seconds.
- cache warm hit-rate: KV cache hits / lookups across model hosts.

Quick reference commands (examples)
- Scale pool +10%: infra-cli pool adjust --pool-id $POOL --scale +10
- Route to fallback variant: routerctl route set --route $RT --variant fallback-v2
- Throttle ingress: rate-limitctl set --route $RT --qps 60%

Open questions / follow-ups (work items)
- Add automated MC runs to daily CI with flagged regressions (owner: product-ops).
- Define synthetic cohort that mimics 3rd-party integrations and test webhook backpressure (owner: solutions-eng).
- Add step to simulate KV cold-start beyond single region (owner: serving-runtime).

Appendix: sample Monte Carlo snippet (excerpt)
- median-p95-latency(Stage D) = 430ms, 75th = 560ms, 95th = 920ms (500 trials).
- median-error-rate(Stage D) = 0.35% (95th = 1.2%).

Notes and versioning
- v0.1 (2025-03-02): initial draft for stakeholder review.
- v0.2 (2025-03-12): added automated rollback thresholds and staffing plan.

Checklist: readiness signals to capture during every soak window (literal telemetry keys)
- telemetry:service.p95_ms, telemetry:service.error_rate, telemetry:autoscaler.actions, telemetry:cache.hit_rate, telemetry:queue.length

End of doc
